ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: The account’s biggest missed opportunity is in the two Non-Brand Search campaigns, where impression share is low (33–35%) and loss is primarily to rank (51% lost to rank in both). Budgets are not currently the binding constraint (budget utilization only ~65–66% across these campaigns), and multiple high-quality keywords still show very high rank loss (64–70% lost to rank despite QS 7.0–8.5), pointing to ad rank/bid/coverage issues rather than capped budgets. Secondary leakage comes from competitor-brand “zero-click” queries consuming nearly half of observed search-term impressions (48.5%), plus a small but fixable set of negative-keyword conflicts blocking ~1,790 impressions.
notable_patterns: Both in-scope Non-Brand campaigns have low search impression share (Flights 33%, Hotels & Packages 35%) with the majority of loss coming from rank (51% lost to rank in each) while budget utilization sits at ~65.7–65.8%, suggesting budget isn’t what’s stopping scale.

High-quality keywords are still failing to win auctions: e.g., "flights to spain" (QS 8.5) has only 34% impression share with 66% lost to rank; "cheap flights europe" (QS 7.5) has 30% impression share with 70% lost to rank.

Query mix includes heavy competitor-brand exposure that appears unproductive: 10,640 competitor-brand zero-click impressions, and 48.5% of search-term impressions in the sample come from zero-click competitor terms; only 0.5 conversions are shown from a competitor-brand term ("trailmark travel quote").

There are efficiency drags tied to low quality score terms with poor outcomes: "flight booking customer service" (QS 4.0) spent £383.76 at £239.85 cost/conv; "hotel cancellation policy" (QS 4.5) spent £329.56 at £205.98 cost/conv.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Search impression share is only 33% with 51% lost to rank vs 16% lost to budget, while budget utilization is just 65.7%—you’re leaving demand on the table primarily because ad rank isn’t high enough, not because the campaign is budget-capped. This lines up with strong-intent keywords like "cheap flights europe" (QS 7.5) still at 30% IS and 70% lost to rank.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase ad rank on the highest-intent non-brand flight terms (bid/target adjustments and tighter query-to-ad-group alignment), while excluding/isolating support-intent queries (e.g., customer service) that dilute performance and QS.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Search impression share is 35% with 51% lost to rank (only 14% lost to budget) and budget utilization at 65.8%, indicating rank is limiting scale. High-intent terms like "all inclusive holidays" (QS 8.0) still show only 36% IS and 64% lost to rank, and there’s also a negative conflict blocking 1,150 impressions tied to a "visa" negative.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Prioritize rank improvements on top converting themes (packages/city breaks) and resolve the "visa" negative conflict by restructuring negatives (e.g., phrase/exact) so non-visa travel intent isn’t inadvertently suppressed.

recommendation_cards.title: Win back Non-Brand impression share by fixing rank on high-QS, high-intent terms
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: The two Non-Brand campaigns are losing the majority of available auctions to rank (51% lost to rank in Flights and 51% in Hotels & Packages) while budget utilization is only ~65.7–65.8%. Even strong terms are under-serving due to rank: "flights to spain" (QS 8.5) sits at 34% impression share with 66% lost to rank; "cheap flights europe" (QS 7.5) is at 30% IS with 70% lost to rank; "all inclusive holidays" (QS 8.0) is at 36% IS with 64% lost to rank.
recommended_steps: Create a short list of 5–10 highest-intent, high-QS keywords/themes (including: "flights to spain", "cheap flights europe", "all inclusive holidays", "weekend city breaks") and apply targeted bid/goal adjustments to raise ad rank specifically on these segments.
Tighten ad-group/theme mapping for these keywords (separate them from broader/adverse intent queries) so the best ads and landing pages serve consistently, improving expected CTR and rank stability.
Monitor impression share lost to rank weekly; keep changes focused on the non-brand campaigns until lost-to-rank materially drops.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Non-Brand Search impression share moving from 33–35% toward 45%+ while impression share lost to rank declines from 51% toward <40%.

recommendation_cards.title: Stop competitor-brand “zero-click” leakage with targeted exclusions or separate handling
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Competitor-brand zero-click queries account for 10,640 impressions and represent 48.5% of the observed search-term impressions, yet only 0.5 conversions are shown from competitor-brand terms ("trailmark travel quote"). This is a large share of attention that is unlikely to scale efficiently in non-brand campaigns.
recommended_steps: Add competitor brand terms shown in the search-term evidence ("skyline journeys", "coastal getaways", "horizon holidays") as negatives in the Non-Brand campaigns to prevent future bleed.
If conquesting is strategically required, isolate it into its own campaign/ad groups with capped bids and tailored ads/landing pages so it cannot suppress core non-brand efficiency.
Re-check the search terms after 7–10 days to confirm competitor-brand impression volume materially decreases and core non-brand themes gain share.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Share of impressions from competitor-brand zero-click terms falling from 48.5% to <15%, with non-brand core themes gaining impressions at similar or better ROAS.

recommendation_cards.title: Eliminate low-QS, support-intent spend that is inflating CPA and dragging rank
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Two low-quality queries/themes are absorbing spend with very poor efficiency: "flight booking customer service" (QS 4.0) spent £383.76 at £239.85 cost/conv, and "hotel cancellation policy" (QS 4.5) spent £329.56 at £205.98 cost/conv. These are typically support/service intents that can depress overall auction performance in mixed ad groups.
recommended_steps: Add intent negatives around support/service where appropriate (e.g., "customer service", "cancellation policy") in acquisition-focused non-brand campaigns, or move these queries into a separate support campaign with constrained bids.
Audit the ad groups where these queries are entering; tighten match types and add query sculpting to keep acquisition ad groups focused on booking intent.
After exclusions/restructure, reallocate saved spend toward the highest-intent non-brand themes that are currently losing 64–70% to rank.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Cost/conv on non-brand decreasing (directionally) while average quality score trends up from 5.5 (Flights) and impression share lost to rank declines.

recommendation_cards.title: Resolve the two negative-keyword conflicts blocking your own demand
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: There are 2 negative conflicts blocking an estimated 1,790 impressions: a "jobs" negative blocking "flight attendant jobs cheap flights europe" (640 impressions) and a "visa" negative blocking "weekend city breaks visa requirements" (1,150 impressions). Regardless of intent quality, these are misconfigurations where account-level negatives are overriding keyword coverage unintentionally.
recommended_steps: In the negative-keyword conflicts report, change the conflicting negatives to more precise forms (e.g., exact/phrase) and/or apply them only in the campaign/ad group where they are truly needed.
If the blocked queries are undesirable, add explicit positives/negatives that prevent collateral blocking (e.g., keep "jobs" exclusions but avoid suppressing broader "cheap flights europe" coverage).
Re-run the conflicts check after changes to confirm blocked impressions return to expected routing.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Blocked impressions reduced from ~1,790 toward 0, with no increase in clearly irrelevant query volume (jobs/immigration-intent) in acquisition campaigns.

already_working: Brand is highly profitable and not the main growth lever: Brand Search - UK delivers ROAS 44.51 on £8,410.92 spend with 594.9 conversions; while it has 20% lost to rank, it’s not where the material missed impressions are (29,400 missed impressions vs 300k+ in non-brand).
Ad creative coverage is strong overall: 83.3% of ads are rated Good or Excellent (4 Excellent, 1 Good), so the immediate bottleneck is more rank/query mix than a broad lack of viable ads.

Head-to-head presence is generally competitive at the auction level: avg top-of-page rate is 66.3% for the account vs 53.9% for competitors, and outranking share is 61.4%, implying the biggest gains will come from lifting rank specifically in non-brand high-intent areas rather than fixing a systemic inability to show at the top.

market_mapping.why_now_summary: You’re currently leaving meaningful non-brand demand unserved primarily due to ad-rank limitations (not budget caps) at a time when the UK travel search market is heating up. External market data shows rapid QoQ search spend growth in the UK, which typically intensifies auctions and raises the cost of waiting: if you don’t address rank loss now, you risk ceding incremental impression share to competitors as demand and spend rise. At the same time, your overall impression share is already slightly below the UK vertical benchmark, reinforcing that there is headroom to capture—especially by fixing rank on high-intent terms rather than adding budget blindly.

email_copy.subject: GBP 254,019 this quarter is stuck behind 47.0% rank loss
email_copy.hook:
Your non-brand campaigns are set up to scale, but they’re not getting the chance: both are only showing ~1 in 3 eligible searches while your daily budget (GBP 6,200) isn’t the thing holding them back.

What jumps out is how consistently you’re being filtered out by ad rank—especially on high-intent terms that should be driving incremental bookings.
why_now_bullets: UK travel auctions are heating up: market QoQ search spend growth is 22.0%, while your account is already sitting at 37.84% impression share (below the 40.0% vertical benchmark).
The market benchmark is 40.0% impression share, but you’re currently giving up 47.0% of available impressions to rank—meaning competitors can take the new demand before you do.
Demand is rising on the exact themes you’re trying to win: market demand for “flights to spain” is +51% (100 to 151), while your account-level impression share lost to rank is still 47.0%.
email_copy.stat_sub: This is recoverable demand being left on the table today.
email_copy.impact_line: Across your two non-brand campaigns, impression share is being capped by rank—not spend: you’re losing 47.0% to rank versus just 15.2% to budget, even with a daily budget of GBP 6,200. In plain terms, you have room to capture more qualified volume right now—if we fix the rank and query mix that’s suppressing coverage.
email_copy.scope_intro: Below is the campaign-by-campaign view of where the missed demand is concentrated, so you can see exactly where the upside is coming from.
email_copy.cards_intro: Here’s the tight, prioritized set of fixes that will unlock impression share quickly—starting with rank on high-intent non-brand, then removing the leakage that’s quietly absorbing your auctions.
email_copy.working_intro: The good news: a few fundamentals are already strong, so we’re not talking about a rebuild—just removing the constraints that are keeping non-brand from scaling.
email_copy.opportunity_intro: If we simply move impression share from 37.84% toward 40.0% at today’s 4.00% click rate, the account adds an estimated 30,240 impressions and 1,209 clicks—one of the cleanest paths to realizing that GBP 254,019 this quarter.
email_copy.fix_title: Want me to map this to a 14-day action plan?
email_copy.fix_body: Are you free Tue 11:00 or Thu 15:00 (UK time) to walk through the quick wins and lock the sequence? If easier, reply “Tue” or “Thu”—or just “plan” and I’ll send the 14-day rollout in writing.
email_copy.ps: P.S. I’m not suggesting “add budget” here—your biggest gains come from fixing rank and filtering out the queries that are currently diluting it.
